title: A trade deal tied garment export quotas to working conditions
body: Cambodia and the US signed a textile and apparel agreement in 1999. It offered higher US import quotas for improvements in working conditions. The ILO began a factory monitoring programme in Cambodia in 2001.
takeaway: A trade quota can be used to set incentives beyond the amount a country may export.
source: World Bank, Better Human Resource Policies in Apparel and Cambodia Trade Agreement
visual: fabric rolls beside an inspection table in a Cambodian garment factory

title: Power lines nearby did not guarantee connections in a Kenyan trial
body: In 2016 researchers reported on a field experiment that varied the cost of connecting rural Kenyan households to the electricity grid. Demand dropped sharply as the price of connecting rose.
takeaway: Building a network and making the last connection affordable are separate problems.
source: Lee, Miguel and Wolfram, NBER Working Paper 22292 (2016)
